_comment: Tool policy for the self-briefing planner quartermaster.sh runs unattended.
The planner's prompt embeds a Linear ticket description — text any
workspace member can edit — and runs with nobody watching, so the policy
is deny-by-default and the allow list is deliberately tiny: everything
absent from `allow` fails immediately rather than prompting, so nothing
blocks waiting for a human who is asleep.
No Bash at all. Permission patterns match the head of a command line and
cannot see what it goes on to execute or write: an allow-listed find can
-exec anything, rg can --pre anything, and cat/jq can redirect anywhere,
which would hand a poisoned description exactly the shell a deny list
pretends to close. Research is Read/Grep/Glob; nothing more is needed to
write a brief.
No Task either. A subagent is a second context with a turn budget of its
own — the ration --max-turns exists to impose, handed out again — and it
reads the same description with none of the caller's suspicion. Whatever
a subagent could research, the planner can research itself.
There is deliberately no file-write rule in allow, and adding one back
would be a mistake. The planner writes its brief into a scratch directory
that quartermaster.sh creates per call and hands it as its working
directory; acceptEdits permits writes inside that tree, and the harness
copies the result out. An allow rule cannot express this — the path is
minted per call — and a rule is not what confines the write anyway: Claude
Code refuses edits outside the session's cwd tree, and refuses edits under
~/.claude entirely as a protected path, whatever this file says. Those two
walls are why the old Write(~/.claude/harness/runs/**) rule could never
work: runs/ lives under ~/.claude, so every self-brief failed as 'planner
wrote no brief', silently, from the day it shipped until 2026-08-10.
Spelling it Edit(path) would not have helped — the wall is the path, not
the tool name. The planner's write reach is now one empty scratch dir
rather than all of runs/, which is strictly tighter than what this file
used to ask for. What it gives up is nothing: quartermaster.sh asks for a
uniquely named, non-armable candidate, publishes it with an atomic
no-clobber link, and checkpoints every brief.md before the planner starts
so it can quarantine and restore writes elsewhere — and 'elsewhere' is now
unreachable anyway.
Edit(~/.claude/**) in deny is the belt to that brace. The confinement above
rests on a Claude Code behaviour this repo does not own, so the harness's
own tree is refused by policy as well: a future release that relaxes the cwd
wall must not silently hand the planner every brief under runs/. It is
scoped to a path on purpose. File permission checks consult Edit rules for
writes whatever tool name asks, so a *bare* Edit here would cover Write in
the scratch dir too and put self-briefing straight back in the hole it just
climbed out of — which is exactly what the old deny list did. The scratch
dir is minted under TMPDIR, so this rule never reaches it. The rest of the
deny list is belt to the same braces: a rule added to allow later cannot
re-open the shell or network paths without also deleting a deny.
The harness's own secrets are denied by path. The planner has no way to
send anything anywhere itself — the network tools are denied above — but
the brief it writes is read by an implementer whose settings do allow Bash
and WebFetch, so a secret quoted into a brief is a secret one step from
leaving the machine. These paths assume the default HARNESS_DIR; a key
kept elsewhere (LINEAR_API_KEY_FILE) needs its own deny.
Read is what this closes. Grep and Glob take a search root rather than a
file path and are matched by tool name only, so treat the deny as the
brake it is, not as proof — what confines the planner is that nothing it
reads has a way out of this machine.
